Spring_MVC_Controller.Description: Traditional Spring web controller used in Spring MVC applications.
Spring_MVC_Controller.Configuration: Requires manual setup (XML or Java-based configuration).
Spring_MVC_Controller.Response_Type: Returns a view (e.g., JSP, Thymeleaf) using a ViewResolver.
Spring_MVC_Controller.Usage: Used for traditional web applications that render HTML views.

Spring_Boot_Controller.Description: Simplified web controller in Spring Boot with built-in configuration.
Spring_Boot_Controller.Configuration: Auto-configured with an embedded server (Tomcat, Jetty, etc.).
Spring_Boot_Controller.Response_Type: Returns data directly (JSON, String, etc.) without a ViewResolver.
Spring_Boot_Controller.Usage: Used for RESTful APIs and microservices.

Key_Differences.Configuration: Spring MVC requires manual setup, while Spring Boot auto-configures components.
Key_Differences.Response_Handling: Spring MVC returns views, while Spring Boot returns data directly.
Key_Differences.View_Resolver: Needed in Spring MVC but not in Spring Boot.
Key_Differences.Embedded_Server: Spring MVC requires external servers; Spring Boot has an embedded server.
